newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai Petroleum Co details drilling operations.
newsitem.headline: Dubai Petroleum Co details drilling operations.

text.p: Dubai Petroleum Company (DPC) continued to drill at its four oilfields last year to maintain the Gulf Arab emirate's modest oil output, according to DPC's 1996 annual review received on Monday.
DPC operates the offshore Fateh, Southwest Fateh, Falah and Rashid fields -- which make up the Dubai blend benchmark crude -- on behalf of the Dubai government.
DPC gave no figures in its review on current or historic production rates which industry sources say run at 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) compared to peak of 410,000 bpd in 1991.
It carried out well work at the main Fateh field which has 118 active oil wells and 69 active water injection wells.
"During 1996, 7 wells were drilled and completed; there were 7 recompletions and 8 wells on which remedial work was done," the DPC annual review reported.

"The miscible gasflood pilot project in Fateh Field commenced in 1993, was concluded in 1996 and continues to help optimize and guide the drilling locations in both Fateh and Southwest Fateh," it said.
Three wells were drilled at Southwest Fateh last year.

"The first and second Mishrif reservoir horizontal wells (CC-9 and NN-18) were drilled and completed and had results better than expected while the first horizontal well to be drilled in the Ilam reservoir (OO-9) is still being tested," the report said.
Development project Falah D, the first to use horizontal oil producers and water injectors, also continued in 1996.

Falah D-10 producer and FC-15W water injector were drilled and completed in 1996 and two horizontal wells were completed in the Falah B development (FB-18 and FB-19) "with very promising results," the review noted.
No significant work was carried out at the Rashid field, the smallest of DPC's fields.

Dubai is one of the seven emirates of OPEC-member United Arab Emirates and is the country's second largest oil producer behind Abu Dhabi which contributes the bulk of UAE's supply quota of 2.161 million bpd.
